subject: Post-call: BrightLeaf usage surge + new RAG / ML workload next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Michael Stone <michael.stone@brightleafhealth.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: BrightLeaf usage surge + RAG / new ML workloads — next steps

Michael / Sara — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap while items are fresh and to align on next steps.

TL;DR
- BrightLeaf is seeing a 2.5x spike in token usage tied to the new triage assistant; growth expected to continue through Q3.
- Top priorities: reduce per-token cost on high-throughput inference, enable a private RAG pipeline for PHI-filtered notes, and pilot embeddings for semantic search across 50M records.
- Suggested expansion path: 1) short Dedicated pilot for RAG (4 weeks), 2) embeddings pilot (6 weeks parallel), 3) production rollout with reserved capacity and SLA.

Pain points we heard
- Latency during peak triage hours (~1200 concurrent requests) spikes to 900–1,100 ms.
- Current hosted provider throttling and opaque pricing on cached tokens.
- Compliance: need KMS-backed key control and audit logs for patient data access.

Goals confirmed
- Target 200–400 ms 95th percentile for triage assistant (user-facing).
- Sub-$0.0006 per token equivalent for cooled workloads (batch embedding generation).
- Auditability for RAG sources and retention policy configurable per dataset.

Proposed immediate actions (owners & timeline)
1) Technical scoping call with Markus to validate RAG architecture and KV-cache requirements (Markus / by 2027-04-26).
2) Provide usage export and cost model break-down for your current Q1 traffic (Vanessa / by 2027-04-23) — attached export.
3) Draft pilot SOW for Dedicated RAG pilot and embeddings evaluation (Grace + Vanessa / by 2027-04-28).
4) Procurement checklist & initial pricing ballpark for pilot and 12-month reserved commit (Vanessa / by 2027-04-25).

Attachments: BrightLeaf_RAG_requirements.pdf (RAG spec you shared), usage_export_Q1_2027.csv (raw usage), redwood_pilot_statement_of_work.docx (initial draft to come).

Questions for you
- Can procurement confirm whether a 12-month committed pricing path is acceptable as soon as pilots demonstrate latency improvements?
- Any regulatory constraints beyond HIPAA we should surface now?

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the Markus scoping session. Thanks — excited to help tighten latency and cost for the triage flow.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
[Attachment: usage_export_Q1_2027.csv (CSV, 1.2 MB)]

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BrightLeaf usage surge + RAG / new ML workloads — next steps

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the write-up, that looks right from our side. A few clarifications: 

1) Procurement: we can commit to a 12-month path if the pilot shows consistent 30–40% cost savings and the SLA holds. I looped them in above.
2) Regulatory: HIPAA is primary; we also have provincial PIPEDA considerations for our Canadian dataset.
3) Timeline: the triage assistant load will peak in early June; having pilot insights before May 20 would be ideal.

Two asks before the scoping call:
- Can you share a short example SLO table we would run during the pilot (latency, P99, error rate)?
- Any blocker to using our managed KMS (AWS KMS) with Redwood private deployment?

Sara — if you have any additional constraints feel free to add.

Thanks — Michael
Chief Product Officer | BrightLeaf Health
[michael.stone@brightleafhealth.com]

Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BrightLeaf usage surge + RAG / new ML workloads — next steps

Appreciate the quick reply, Michael — answers inline below and attaching the SLO template.

- 12-month commit: understood; we'll produce a pilot pricing path and a conservative reserved-commit proposal for procurement to review by 2027-04-25.
- Regulatory: noted PIPEDA — Markus, please note when we scope data residency and logging.

Attached: pilot_SLO_table.csv (simple SLOs) and an updated short pilot checklist.

Quick answers: 
- SLOs: 95th pct latency target for triage = 200–350 ms (depends on model size/quantization). P99 targets are workable but will need Dedicated pilot telemetry to guarantee. We'll use error rate <0.5% for production readiness.
- KMS: AWS KMS integration is supported for Private deployments (customer-managed keys), we will validate key-wrap flow during Markus's scoping call. For hosted Redwood, KMS-backed encryption is available via shared services but we recommend Private for PHI.

Next: I'll send a calendar invite for the scoping call (45 min) for Monday 2027-04-26 at 10:00 PT — Markus please confirm availability.

Thanks — Vanessa
[Attachment: pilot_SLO_table.csv (CSV, 2 KB)]

Thanks Vanessa — I can take the scoping session Monday and will prepare the following before we meet: 

1) Feasibility notes (one page) covering: model sizing options (quantized LLM variants), expected 95th latency per bucket, and tradeoffs for KV cache sizing.
2) Pilot architecture sketch (diagram link to Drive) showing Dedicated GPU pool + Private control plane for RAG ingestion and KMS integration.
3) SLO table (concrete numbers) and a lightweight telemetry plan we can run during the 4-week pilot.

Initial observations:
- With a 4-GPU Dedicated pool (A10G-equivalent) and continuous batching tuned for prompt length ~320 tokens, we should hit ~250–350 ms P95 for an optimized quantized 13B model. If BrightLeaf wants sub-200ms P95 consistently, we should consider 8-GPU or smaller model ensembles + aggressive KV cache hit rates.
- Embeddings for 50M records: recommend staged ingestion (10M increments) with incremental dedup and sampling. We'll size storage/throughput and propose a parallel batch runner to keep costs controlled.

I'll upload the draft diagram and feasibility note to the Drive folder and share ahead of Monday's call.

Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
